AcceptAttestationRequest.description: Countersign a pending attestation. Must be called by a wallet holding the subject profile's user token.

ActionType.description: A TAGGED object, not a constructor-keyed one: the arm's name is in "tag" and its own fields sit beside it. Shapes: ProfileAction: "contents" is ProfileActionType; DisputeAction: "contents" is DisputeActionType; ProtocolAction: "contents" is ProtocolActionType; AdminAction: "contents". The AdminAction arm carries [AdminActionType, ClaimWitness or null] — the action, and how the current admin proves control of a script credential (ADR 0005). It is NOT accepted in a request body — it is a 400. Those actions are built and signed by the admin CLI, which holds the credential the oracle validator requires.

contents.description: The arm's payload. Its schema depends on "tag" — see the shapes in this schema's description.

tag.description: Which arm of the union this object is.

AdminActionType.description: NOT ACCEPTED OVER HTTP — every request body carrying an admin action is a 400. These actions change oracle parameters and the oracle validator requires the admin's signature, so a service can only ever return an unsigned transaction; they are built and signed by the admin CLI. Listed because the action union has an arm for them.

AttestationType.description: What an attestation asserts about its subject: milestone_delivered (a budget administrator attests a vendor's delivery), audit_passed (an auditor attests it reviewed one), affiliation (organisation to member, usually with a claimed period), role_held (an extra-chain mandate such as a working-group lead or committee chair, usually with a claimed period), endorsement, credential_claim (a profile binds itself to a Cardano governance credential, which is what the `credential` field of a profile is derived from) and credential_withdrawal (that binding ended). For the first five the kind is presentational: it says what a reader is being told, not what the protocol permits. The last two the protocol does enforce — they must be self-issued and must name a credential that proved control of the minting transaction, and the first five must name none.

ClaimCredentialRequest.description: Bind a profile to a Cardano credential, as an append-only record. Needs BOTH parties: the returned transaction spends the profile's user token and must be authorised by the credential as well. Costs a second transaction after /claim-profile, and buys a binding that can be ended by appending a withdrawal rather than by clearing a field.

ClaimProfileRequest.description: Mint a profile. It claims no credential: since ADR 0003 a binding is its own record, so bind the profile with POST /claim-credential afterwards. `recipient` receives any unlocked funds and defaults to the change address.

image_uri.description: URI of the profile image (the client hosts it; the protocol stores the URI)

ClaimWitness.description: How control of the claimed credential is proven. One of {"tag": "key"}, {"tag": "simple_script", "script": <native script>}, or {"tag": "plutus_script", "script": "<script CBOR hex>", "redeemer": <script data>}.

DisputeActionType.description: A TAGGED object, not a constructor-keyed one: the arm's name is in "tag" and its own fields sit beside it. Shapes: OpenDisputeAction: od_attestation_id, od_opened_by_profile_id, od_deposit_to, od_profile_data; ResolveDisputeAction: rd_dispute_id, rd_verdict; ExpireDisputeAction: ed_dispute_id.

tag.description: Which arm of the union this object is.

ExpireDisputeRequest.description: Close an undecided dispute whose deadline has passed, naming it by `dispute_id`. No verdict and no authority: the transaction this returns needs only a fee payer, and it records the dispute as `expired`, which is NOT a finding against either party. The deposit returns to the address the opener named. A dispute that is already decided, or whose deadline has not passed, is a 400.

GYAddress.description: Cardano address as RAW CBOR HEX (114 hex characters), not bech32: this field is parsed with deserialiseFromRawBytesHex, so addr_test1…/addr1… is refused. `admin operator-address` prints the hex form.

GYAssetClass.description: Cardano native asset identifier in format: <56-char policy ID hex>.<asset name hex>

InteractionStatusResponse.description: Which provider and network this service is configured against, whether its reference scripts resolve, whether the protocol is paused, and the oracle's mutable parameters. `oracle` is the ONLY published source of the registry's own deposit, dispute timeout, minimum UTxO, fees and admin/arbiter credentials — query-api's `epoch_params` is the LEDGER's protocol parameters and a different thing. Always 200: /ready is the route that fails.

IssueAttestationRequest.description: Issue an attestation to a profile.

claimed_period.description: Optional [from, to] period the attestation CLAIMS, e.g. the span of an affiliation or a mandate. SELF-REPORTED: no on-chain fact can establish it, so it is never presented as verified, and only its ordering (from <= to) is checked. Both bounds or neither.

items.description: This is the posix time in ISO8601 format.
This is the posix time in ISO8601 format.

image_uri.description: URI of the attestation image (the client hosts it; the protocol stores the URI)

OpenDisputeRequest.description: Open a dispute against an attestation, locking the deposit the oracle currently requires. `attestation_id` is the attestation being contested and `opened_by_profile_id` the disputer, whose user token the wallet must hold. `deposit_to` is where the deposit returns on EITHER verdict. OMIT IT: it then defaults to the address holding the opener's user token, which is the one address the protocol is satisfied by for free, because spending that UTxO is how the opener authorises. If you do name one it must be an address you listed in `user_addresses` — an input from anywhere else would need that holder's signature, which nothing in this flow can produce, so it is refused as `DepositAddressNotSpendable` before anything is built rather than after you sign. A SCRIPT address is refused outright as `DepositAddressIsScript`: the refund is a plain output with no datum, which a script cannot spend, so it would be lost. `recipient` receives any unlocked funds and defaults to the change address.

description.description: What is being contested, and why

image_uri.description: URI of the dispute image (the client hosts it; the protocol stores the URI)

ProfileActionType.description: A TAGGED object, not a constructor-keyed one: the arm's name is in "tag" and its own fields sit beside it. Shapes: UpdateProfileAction: profile_id, new_desc, image_uri; ClaimProfileAction: cp_kind, cp_profile_data; ClaimCredentialAction: cc_profile_id, cc_credential, cc_witness, cc_profile_data; WithdrawCredentialAction: wc_profile_id, wc_credential, wc_witness, wc_profile_data; IssueAttestationAction: aa_subject_profile_id, aa_issuer_profile_id, aa_kind, aa_profile_data, aa_other_metadata, aa_claimed_period; AcceptAttestationAction: aca_attestation_id.

items.description: This is the posix time in ISO8601 format.
This is the posix time in ISO8601 format.

tag.description: Which arm of the union this object is.

ResolveDisputeRequest.description: Settle a dispute, naming it by `dispute_id`. Returns an UNSIGNED transaction: the oracle validator requires the admin's signature, so the admin signs what this route builds. `recipient` receives any unlocked funds and defaults to the change address.

UpdateProfileRequest.description: Update a profile's metadata (description, image). Name is immutable.

description.description: New profile description (omit to keep current)

image_uri.description: URI of the profile image (the client hosts it; the protocol stores the URI)

UserAddresses.description: Wallet addresses used as inputs for transaction building. Provide all UTxO addresses from the connected wallet.

WithdrawCredentialRequest.description: End a profile's binding to a credential. Authorised by the CREDENTIAL alone -- not by the profile's owner, who may be exactly the party that claimed a credential they do not control. Nothing is deleted: the claim stays on chain and this record is appended beside it, after which the read layer stops publishing the binding.

credential.description: The CIP-129 identifier being withdrawn. A withdrawal naming a different credential than the profile currently publishes changes nothing.

info.description: This is the Palmares Interaction API — transaction building, submission, and the dedicated per-action service endpoints.
info.title: Palmares Interaction API

post.description: Accepts a pending attestation; only the subject's wallet can do this.

200.description: Success. The write routes return the hex-encoded unsigned transaction CBOR — sign it with your wallet and submit it via /submit-tx; the probe, status and tx-status routes return the JSON object their schema names.

400.description: Validation error (invalid dates, wrong profile type, conflicting state, etc.)

401.description: No credentials, or credentials that could not be read. Code: unauthenticated. The response carries a WWW-Authenticate challenge naming the Basic realm; send HTTP Basic credentials.

403.description: Credentials were supplied and are not accepted. Code: credentials_rejected. This is an authentication failure under a 403 because that is the status servant's BasicAuth answers with; it is NOT a permission check, and this API has none.

404.description: Referenced entity not found (profile, attestation, or NFT), or no route matches the path. Code: route_not_found for the latter, a TxBuildingException tag for the former.

405.description: Wrong HTTP method for this path. Code: method_not_allowed. Every write route is a POST; /health, /ready, /status and /tx-status are GETs.

406.description: The Accept header asked for a media type this service does not produce; it serves application/json only. Code: not_acceptable.

415.description: The request body was not sent as application/json. Set Content-Type: application/json. Code: unsupported_media_type.

500.description: A bug here, never a condition the request can fix: an unclassified failure (InternalError, or internal_error from the last-resort handler), or a datum this protocol wrote and cannot now parse (OracleDatumInvalid, DatumParseError).

502.description: The chain provider could not be reached, or the node rejected the submission. Code: ProviderError. The request was well formed and may be worth retrying.

503.description: Protocol is paused or deployed validator scripts are not yet available

404.description: Referenced entity not found (profile, attestation, or NFT), or no route matches the path. Code: route_not_found for the latter, a TxBuildingException tag for the former.

405.description: Wrong HTTP method for this path. Code: method_not_allowed. Every write route is a POST; /health, /ready, /status and /tx-status are GETs.

406.description: The Accept header asked for a media type this service does not produce; it serves application/json only. Code: not_acceptable.

415.description: The request body was not sent as application/json. Set Content-Type: application/json. Code: unsupported_media_type.

500.description: A bug here, never a condition the request can fix: an unclassified failure (InternalError, or internal_error from the last-resort handler), or a datum this protocol wrote and cannot now parse (OracleDatumInvalid, DatumParseError).

502.description: The chain provider could not be reached, or the node rejected the submission. Code: ProviderError. The request was well formed and may be worth retrying.

503.description: Protocol is paused or deployed validator scripts are not yet available

post.description: Ends a profile's binding to a credential. Authorised by the CREDENTIAL alone — not by the profile's owner, who may be exactly the party that claimed a credential they do not control. Nothing is deleted: the claim stays on chain and this record is appended beside it.

200.description: Success. The write routes return the hex-encoded unsigned transaction CBOR — sign it with your wallet and submit it via /submit-tx; the probe, status and tx-status routes return the JSON object their schema names.

400.description: Validation error (invalid dates, wrong profile type, conflicting state, etc.)
